places.what: Born in the family’s white-painted house at Strandgaten 152, just above the Vågen harbour. Coordinates mark Bergen, not the house.

places.name: Landås, Bergen
places.what: At the family’s summer house in the summer of 1858 the violinist Ole Bull heard the boy play and told him: “You are going to Leipzig to become an artist!”

places.name: Leipzig
places.what: Admitted to the Conservatory on 6 October 1858; saw Tannhäuser fourteen times, fell ill with tuberculosis in 1860 and graduated in the spring of 1862.

places.name: Copenhagen
places.what: Went with a loan from his father; met Niels Gade in the summer of 1863 and later Rikard Nordraak; became engaged to his cousin Nina Hagerup in 1864.

places.name: Rome
places.what: His first Italian stay, kept in a diary. He met Ibsen at the Scandinavian Club and wrote a funeral march when news came that Nordraak had died in Berlin on 20 March 1866.

sources.title: Finn Benestad: Edvard Grieg, Norsk biografisk leksikon

places.name: Berlin
places.what: Visited Nordraak’s grave and took an oak leaf from it, which he enclosed in a long letter to Nordraak’s father.

places.name: Christiania (Oslo)
places.what: Conducted the Philharmonic Society, started a music academy with Otto Winter-Hjelm and, in 1871, founded the Musikforeningen. Left the capital in 1874.

places.name: Copenhagen
places.what: Married his cousin Nina Hagerup in St John’s Church (Johanneskirken); neither set of parents attended. The couple left at once for Christiania.

places.name: Søllerød
places.what: Stayed at Søllerød, north of Copenhagen, from June 1868 and wrote the Piano Concerto in A minor there; Nina and baby Alexandra stayed with Nina’s parents.

places.name: Copenhagen
places.what: First performance of the Piano Concerto in A minor, with Edmund Neupert as soloist and Holger Simon Paulli conducting. Neupert wrote that the audience broke into a storm after the first-movement cadenza.

sources.title: Finn Benestad: Edvard Grieg, Norsk biografisk leksikon
Wikipedia coordinate record: Copenhagen

places.name: Rome
places.what: Visited Liszt twice. At the second meeting Liszt played the manuscript of the Piano Concerto at sight, and told him to carry on.

places.name: Bayreuth
places.what: Attended the first Bayreuth Festival, where Wagner’s Ring was staged complete, and wrote eight reports for the Bergen newspaper Bergensposten.

places.name: Christiania (Oslo)
places.what: Peer Gynt, with Grieg’s music, opened at the Christiania Theatre. It ran thirty-six times that spring; the theatre burned down on 15 January 1877.

places.name: Ullensvang, Hardanger
places.what: Settled at the farm Øvre Børve in late June 1877 and moved before winter to Lofthus, where he built a small work-hut that locals called “Komposten”. Wrote the String Quartet in G minor in Hardanger. Coordinates mark the Ullensvang district, not Lofthus village or the hut.

places.what: Settled in Bergen in the spring of 1880 and became conductor of the Harmonien society that autumn, a post he held for two years.

places.what: Met Tchaikovsky at the home of the violinist Adolph Brodsky. Tchaikovsky later inscribed his Hamlet overture to him.

places.name: Jotunheimen
places.what: A summer trip that freed his creative energy again. On a mountain farm he heard the dairymaid Gjendine Slaalien sing the “Gjendines bådnlåt”, the only tune he wrote down himself.

places.name: Cambridge
places.what: Received the honorary Doctor of Music in person; he had been too ill to attend in June 1893, when Tchaikovsky, Saint-Saëns, Bruch and Boito were honoured.

places.name: Paris
places.what: Returned after the Dreyfus quarrel of 1899. On 19 April he conducted at the Concerts Colonne; whistles and shouts of “À bas Dreyfus” sent him off the podium until the police had cleared the worst of the hall, and the concert ended as a triumph. On 2 May he recorded nine sides for the Gramophone and Typewriter Company.
